_what: How the uploader paces itself so it moves like a person in Ads Manager, not a script (the owner, 21 Oct 2026: "think through actual human-like movement for this uploading process … it's not human the way we're uploading these massive files"). Read by pace.py. Seconds unless named. Set META_PACE=off only in tests.
_why: 21 Oct 2026: three 6-minute song ads (five ~350 MB versions each) went up back to back, ~3 GB in under an hour; Meta's video server answered 503 and the uploader quit on the first one.
_per_hour_why: 11 Nov 2026: videos per hour 8 -> 16 (owner: more video ads per hour); files are now filed at 4 Mbps (delivery.py), so the 1.2 GB/hour byte cap that stopped Meta's 503s (21 Oct) stays as it was. Rollback: videos 8.

usage._what: Meta's own usage meters, read from every reply's headers (x-business-use-case-usage, x-ad-account-usage, x-app-usage). At slow_at % on any meter the uploader adds a pause before each call, longer as it climbs; at pause_at % (or when Meta names a time to regain access) it waits that time, at least pause_min_s, before the next call. 11 Nov 2026: both ad accounts report ads_api_access_tier development_access; a ten-video card hit code 17 / 2446079.

_per_hour_link: A video Meta fetches by link (upload-link.json) counts toward per_hour.videos but not per_hour.bytes: the bytes cap guards Meta's video server against our pushes (21 Oct), and a link sends no bytes from here.
